newsitem.title: USA: Besicorp, CEO indicted for political contributions.
newsitem.headline: Besicorp, CEO indicted for political contributions.

text.p: Besicorp Group Inc. and its chief executive officer were indicted Thursday for conspiring to violate the federal campaign finance laws and making false statements in connection with the 1992 election campaign of Rep. Maurice Hinchey, D-N.Y., federal prosecutors said.

The indictment alleges that Kingston, N.Y.-based Besicorp, which designs, engineers and constructs power plants, and Michael Zinn, the company's executive officer and majority shareholder, made $27,000 in illegal corporate campaign contributions to the Hinchey campaign.
The defendants were indicted in White Plains, N.Y. federal court.

In a statement Besicorp said, "Besicorp and Mr. Zinn vigorously and completely deny all charges contained in this indictment in the strongest possible terms. We intend to take this case to trial and be fully exonerated."
If convicted on all charges, Zinn faces a possible maximum sentence of 25 years in prison and $1.25 million in fines. Besicorp faces a maximum of $1.25 million in fines.
Hinchey was first elected to the House of Representatives in 1992 and has been reelected twice since then. Zinn was the finance chairman for his 1992 campaign.
The indictment charges the contributions were made by reimbursing Besicorp employees and an employee of another company controlled by Zinn for payments they their relatives made to the campaign.
The reimbursements were made to the employees with bonuses, raises and cash.

The indictment also charges that Besicorp and Zinn solicited and received $40,000 in illegal corporate contributions for the Hinchey campaign from Ansaldo North America Inc., the U.S. affiliate of a large Italian company with whom Besicorp was a co-venturer on a number of power plant projects.
The indictment charges that the defendants solicited Ansaldo to have its employees make donations to the Hinchey campaign and then to reimburse those employees for their contributions.
Ansaldo pleaded guilty to related charges in March.
Besicorp said it expects to incur substantial legal fees and expenses.
